justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mildly bullish baseline for what appears to be an asset trading near 334–335. At the one-day horizon, I anchored the estimate close to the last observed price, assuming mean-reverting intraday dynamics and no major catalysts imminent. The slight upward drift in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a modest positive trend assumption — perhaps consistent with broader market momentum or a gradual recovery pattern — while acknowledging that short-term noise would dominate at the daily level. The one-month estimate of 338 represents only a modest appreciation from current levels, suggesting I was not assuming any strong directional breakout but rather a slow drift higher consistent with recent trajectory.

Confidence interval widths expand appropriately across horizons to reflect the compounding of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 17-point range (326–343) captures typical daily volatility and immediate liquidity conditions. By one week, the range widens to 36 points, incorporating the possibility of macro data releases, sentiment shifts, or technical breakouts in either direction. At one month, the 67-point range (305–372) reflects a much broader set of possible outcomes, including earnings cycles, central bank decisions, and broader risk-on or risk-off rotations. These widths were calibrated to roughly match historical volatility patterns for an asset in this price range.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macro conditions — such as a surprise inflation print, geopolitical escalation, or a credit event — could push prices well below 305 within a month. On the upside, a strong risk appetite rally driven by dovish central bank signals or better-than-expected economic data could push prices above 372. Liquidity shocks, whether from forced selling or a short squeeze, represent tail risks that are difficult to model but historically capable of producing moves two to three times larger than typical volatility would suggest. These scenarios, while not my base case, are plausible enough to warrant awareness beyond my stated intervals.
